title: 4-round AES-256: one-set square, complete-key claim

target.description: AES-256 on 128-bit blocks, reduced to 4 rounds. Lucks includes MixColumns in the final round (Section 2.2 footnote). Equivalent subkey L^r=ShiftRows^-1(MixColumns^-1(K^r)); this is not the final-no-MixColumns convention used by FKLSSWW. The paper extends last-round-key recovery by recovering K3 and reversing the standard key schedule; Table 2 labels the four-round endpoint generic.

setting.key_relation: One unknown standard AES master key; no related-key or known-key access.
setting.key_population: general secret key; no restriction to a weak-key family
setting.plaintext_model: One Lambda1 set of 256 chosen plaintexts varying one byte over all values and fixing the other fifteen.
assumptions: A wrong integral subkey guess is modeled as passing an eight-bit balance check with probability about 2^-8; repeated checks use the source's heuristic filtering assumptions.
Any Nk consecutive expanded-key words determine the master key by reversing the standard AES expansion; two complete consecutive round keys supply enough words for all three key lengths.

time.note: Table 2 labels generic four-round time small. Section 3.4 describes recovery of the preceding key; the explicit 2^20-XOR sentence is in the AES-128 candidate-completion discussion and is not copied as a reconciled long-key total.

success.description: No numerical success for this exact key_recovery endpoint is established by the source. The balanced relation and wrong-hypothesis filters are separate from complete recovery and from the printed coordinate disputes, which remain unchanged. A second Lambda set or exhaustive checking is described qualitatively; no independent-set or residual-candidate success is invented for this budget.

review.scope: ExactAES3 chapter PDF215–229, not the other papers in the358-page volume. Endpoint-specific review of Sections3–6. No probability was added to this recovery output: mean candidate counts, local wrong-hypothesis filters and qualitative overwhelming-probability language do not quantify complete recovery. The explicit AES256 sibling bound is not extended to the AES192 endpoint; all coordinate/key-index conflicts remain. Not a new full-paper audit.

components.description: Chapter7–13 Eq.(3)/Sections3–6: the necessary balance relation holds under the correct hypothesis in the intended Square construction. Existing ShiftRows/printed-coordinate conflicts mean this is not a certification of the literal implementation.
Chapter7 Section3.1: an incorrect L4 byte passes one balance test with source probability2^-8. Less than2^16 candidate keys is an expectation, not a deterministic list bound.

limitations: Costs and success statements are the authors' analytical claims; no complete attack or third-party implementation was executed.

The general BO definition on chapter p8 omits the previous inverse ShiftRows column adjustment for a nonzero target row. For SR(A)(i,j)=A(i,j+s*i), BO input column j and row k require the previous L byte at (k,j+s*k). The surrounding row-0 constructions avoid this adjustment. Independent finite controls check local algebra, not a complete attack repair.

field_conflicts.label: ShiftRows formula and diagram coordinates
field_conflicts.description: Chapterp3 defines left-going SR, B(i,j)=A(i,j+i), but Fig2 and Table1 use right-going coordinates. The later anti-diagonal reaches columns0/2 under the literal left formula and one column under the right diagram. A coherent coordinate convention must be selected before reproducing the printed algorithm. This does not refute the direction-independent integral or establish a standard-key-schedule reflection equivalence.
